result:
Solution 1 is internally inconsistent. Its own order-16 check says only 3 of 5 classes are symmetric-equivalent, yet it concludes that all 487 classes at order 28 have symmetric representatives. Its key claim is therefore unsupported and contradicted by its own data, so 487 is wrong.

Solution 2 is not an exact count. It certifies 91 classes and then adds one more from statistical richness estimators (Chao1 and related). Those estimates are heuristics, so 92 cannot be accepted as an exact answer.

Solution 3 gives 91 and describes a concrete route: reduce to the polarity condition (a signed permutation P with HP symmetric), use the known total of 487 Hadamard classes at order 28 as a completeness check, and test polarity by two methods that were validated on smaller orders. I have not reproduced its computations, and I cannot confirm that 91 matches the published count of symmetric classes at order 28. Still, it is the only one of the three whose final number comes from an exact procedure rather than an unsupported claim or a statistical extrapolation, so I judge it the most likely correct answer.

CHOICE: 3
